question: Do conclusions persist when later chronological splits exclude every aircraft identifier observed in earlier splits?

split_rule.date_assignment: Reuse the parent chronological 60/20/20 airport-specific date lists without change.
split_rule.train: Retain every eligible track on train dates.
split_rule.development: Retain only identifiers never observed on train dates.
split_rule.test: Retain only identifiers never observed on train or development dates.
split_rule.identity_visibility: Raw identifiers are used only for filtering; materialized files use compact daily IDs and reports contain counts plus salted-free set hashes, not identifiers.

models: final unweighted Gibbs plus Energy-KL MABPT
evaluation.development_role: sensitivity analysis only; no model or hyperparameter selection
evaluation.test_role: retrospective subgroup analysis after the original locked-test evaluation

failure_criteria: Any retained identifier intersection across train, development, and test
Any change to parent date membership
Any non-finite or non-contiguous materialized track
Fewer than one eligible scene in a later split
claim_boundary: This removes persistent-identifier reuse while preserving chronological dates, but it remains a retrospective local-data sensitivity analysis and may change traffic composition substantially.
